title: Does More Thinking Pay Off? Reasoning Cost and Correctness of LLMs in Code Generation and Bug Fixing
title_zh: 更多思考是否值得？LLM 在代码生成与缺陷修复中的推理成本与正确性

paragraphs.en: 研究显示LLM更多推理并非总是更好，正确率提升有限而token开销显著，应同时报告推理成本。 Many LLMs now emit an explicit reasoning trace before they write code, but benchmark results for code generation and bug fixing usually report correctness alone. It is therefore unclear how much the extra reasoning contributes relative to the tokens it consumes. We examine this question with 866 Python tasks drawn from HumanEval Pro, MBPP Pro, and BugsInPy under five model settings. We look at the accuracy gain and token overhead of reasoning, the behaviors that appear inside reasoning traces, and whether a shortened trace still leads to a correct solution. Turning reasoning on in Qwen3-32B over five runs improves mean pass@1 on HumanEval Pro from 71.1% to 76.5% and mean tests pass on BugsInPy from 3.5% to 7.9%. On MBPP Pro the improvement from 68.1% to 69.5% is not statistically significant, even though the model uses a median of over 2,000 thinking tokens per task. Across models, a longer median trace does not reliably mean higher accuracy. A qualitative analysis shows that traces mostly choose and check an implementation in code generation, while in bug fixing they mostly locate the fault and plan the repair. We then truncate stored traces offline and ask Qwen3-32B with reasoning off to produce a solution from what remains. Retaining the first half of a trace yields no statistically significant drop in correctness. Stopping when the trace becomes repetitive seldom triggers, and stopping once solution code first appears benefits some models but harms others. Neither rule beats plain fixed truncation. These results suggest that more reasoning is not always better and that studies should report reasoning cost alongside correctness.
paragraphs.zh: 研究显示LLM更多推理并非总是更好，正确率提升有限而token开销显著，应同时报告推理成本。许多LLM现在在编写代码之前会输出显式的推理轨迹，但代码生成与缺陷修复的基准测试结果通常只报告正确率。 因此，相对于其消耗的token，额外的推理究竟贡献多少仍不清楚。 我们使用来自HumanEval Pro、MBPP Pro和BugsInPy的866个Python任务，在五种模型设置下考察这一问题。 我们考察推理的准确率提升与token开销、推理轨迹中出现的行为，以及缩短的轨迹是否仍能得到正确的解。 在Qwen3-32B上开启推理并进行五次运行，使HumanEval Pro的平均pass@1从71.1%提升到76.5%，BugsInPy的平均测试通过率从3.5%提升到7.9%。 在MBPP Pro上，从68.1%到69.5%的提升在统计上不显著，尽管该模型每个任务使用的中位数思考token超过2,000个。 跨模型来看，中位数轨迹更长并不必然意味着更高的准确率。 定性分析表明，在代码生成中轨迹主要是选择并检查一种实现，而在缺陷修复中它们主要是定位故障并规划修复方案。 随后我们离线截断已存储的轨迹，并让关闭推理的Qwen3-32B根据剩余内容生成解。 保留轨迹的前一半在正确率上没有统计上显著的下降。 当轨迹变得重复时停止的规则很少触发，而在解代码首次出现时停止的规则对某些模型有益但对另一些模型有害。 这两种规则都不优于简单的固定截断。 这些结果表明，更多推理并非总是更好，研究应在报告正确率的同时报告推理成本。
